Players complete 30 lunar missions through educational minigames, manage resources like oxygen, water, food, and power, and make decisions that affect crew survival.
The game integrates real NASA space-weather data into simulated emergencies and features ORBI, a virtual assistant providing educational facts and hints.
Our project addresses the Junior Astronauts Training challenge by making space science fun and accessible while developing critical thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making skills in future space explorers.
details:
OUTPOST 30: Save Our Moon Base is an interactive lunar survival simulator developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the Junior Astronauts Training challenge. Our target audience is children aged 7–12.

The game features 30 daily missions, each with its own interactive minigame inspired by real astronaut activities. Players manage oxygen, water, food, power, and crew health while making decisions that affect their mission's progress. Unexpected emergencies introduce realistic challenges and encourage problem-solving.

We integrated NASA DONKI space-weather data to incorporate real solar-flare observations into simulated mission scenarios. Our virtual robot assistant, ORBI, provides educational facts, hints, and guidance throughout the experience.

Technologies used: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Three.js, NASA APIs, GitHub, and Vercel for deployment. We also used ChatGPT Plus for development assistance, debugging, and planning.

Our creativity lies in combining educational minigames, interactive 3D exploration, real NASA data, and a decision-based survival system. We considered age-appropriate learning, accessibility, scientific accuracy, engaging gameplay, and realistic resource limitations.

Our intended impact is to inspire young space enthusiasts while developing critical thinking, teamwork, resource management, and decision-making skills through an enjoyable STEM learning experience.
